back: A scale written as a ratio such as 1:50 000; it has no units (1 map unit = 50 000 of the same units on the ground).
1 cm represents 0.5 km; 2 cm represent 1 km; one grid square = 1 km².
1 cm represents 250 m; 4 cm represent 1 km.
Distance = √(ΔE² + ΔN²), with ΔE and ΔN in km (grid lines are 1 km apart).
Pivot a paper edge at each bend, lay string along the route, or step with dividers; then apply the scale.
Count complete squares, add part squares (often as halves); each square = 1 km² on 1:50 000 maps.
A divided line labelled with ground distances; stays correct if the map is enlarged or reduced.
